correctness.rationale: For \(\omega(n)=4\), \(n=2^a p^b q^c r^d\) with \(a\ge2\) and odd \(p<q<r\), \(\sigma^*(n)/n\) equals the product of four terms \(1+1/\text{prime power}\). Unitary Zumkeller forces this product at least 2. Exact monotonic prime-power bounds exclude \(a\ge4\), isolate \(n=840\) at \(a=3\), and yield \(n=60r^e\) or \(84r\) with r=11,13,17,19 at \(a=2\). Unitary partition witnesses are n and 60 (for \(60r^e\)), \(n\) plus listed proper divisors (for \(84r\)), and 840 plus 24. Proper unitary divisor half-sum witnesses are supplied in RESULT.md for every case. The bundled exact integer verifier checks all 5,851 members of the finite test domain through 100000, obtains 274 matching unitary examples, and checks their proper equal partitions. Infinite coverage relies on the inequalities and symbolic witness identities, not the finite census.

value.rationale: The 2024 originating article proposes studying prime-factor structure and conjectures every even unitary Zumkeller number is unitary half-Zumkeller. Exactly four prime supports with valuation at least two form a natural infinite stratum at the second dyadic layer, with both free odd prime powers and genuinely exceptional isolated configurations. This theorem gives a sharp structural iff classification, proves necessary unitary abundance sufficient in the stratum, supplies a sharp power-of-two cutoff, and verifies the proper unitary partition conjecture on the complete stratum. It is not a generic parity check, restated definition or merely a tabulated finite coincidence.
